challenge.better_approach: A build_inspector sieve (call-level, beside sole_path_holds) would be physics on every inspection; import_sieve judges imports, and platform is imported legitimately for platform.system everywhere, so it cannot express this. A proof at the door is smaller now; the sieve is a later hypothesis.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That AST catches every spelling: a subprocess calling `hostname`, or getattr(os, 'uname'), is invisible to it (the same residue CLAUDE.md names for import_sieve). That bash's superclaude:260 is acceptable as a second spelling because bash cannot import the tool.
challenge.prior_art: inferenceproxy/proofs/test_host.py shakes a sole-path rule over the whole repo at its own address; import_sieve's sole_path kind; ticket 5ccc7f05c932 (the door itself).
challenge.real_collision: RULE 1 says a ticket's proofs measure only its component; this proof reads other components' source text. Distinction, not collision: it reaches no code through a back door, it reads files the way the encapsulation sieve does, and the precedent is inferenceproxy's repo-wide mesh.

answers.falsifier: Done when: an AST scan of every Python file under cairn/, skills/ and bin/ (a .py file, or an extensionless file whose first line is a python shebang) finds a call to os.uname, platform.node, platform.uname or socket.gethostname (attribute calls and names bound by from-imports alike) in exactly one file, cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/host/host.py AND the same scanner, run over a scratch tree holding one planted call of each spelling (os.uname().nodename, platform.node(), platform.uname(), and `from socket import gethostname` then gethostname()), reports all four plants, so the scan cannot read green by seeing nothing. Wrong intent if a site genuinely cannot import the tool (runs before cairn is on sys.path) and has to keep its own spelling.

answers.what: Exactly one place in Cairn asks the OS for this box's name: the tool the system device publishes, cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/host/host.py. Every other site asks that tool.
